Because string and number do not overlap: neither is assignable to the other
Because "2500" cannot be converted to a number

questions.q: What makes value as unknown as T compile for any T?

options: TypeScript checks value twice, once for each as
Every type is assignable to unknown, and unknown overlaps with every type, so both steps are allowed
unknown converts the value to T at runtime
It only compiles when T is an interface

const a = { id: "ACC-1" } as Account;
const a = { id: 1, balance: 0 } as Account;
const a = { id: "ACC-1" } satisfies Account;
